did_you_know.text: The phrase “the terebinths of Mamre” probably describes a grove or group of trees, not necessarily one specific tree. Different translations render the Hebrew word as “oak” or “terebinth.”
In the ancient Near East, hospitality usually included water for washing feet, a place to rest, and food. This was especially important for travelers walking dusty roads in sandals.
A seah was an ancient measure of volume, though its exact size is uncertain. Three seahs of flour were still a large amount, showing that Abraham prepared a very generous meal.
The ancient phrase “at this time next year” probably means during the same season the following year. It refers not to a particular hour, but to a set time in the future.
“The way of women” is a polite expression for the menstrual cycle. The verse uses gentle language to explain why Sarah could no longer give birth naturally.
The root of the word “too difficult” is connected with something beyond human ability. The question is not only whether a miracle can happen, but whether anything is impossible for God.

The pairing “righteousness and justice” appears throughout the Bible to describe moral life and a fair society. According to the verse, faith is also tested in daily actions and in the way one treats family members.

The phrase “I will go down and see” presents God using the language of a judge who checks the facts before passing sentence. It emphasizes that punishment is not arbitrary, but connected with investigation and justice.

The question “Will the Judge of all the earth not do justice?” became one of the Bible’s best-known statements about divine justice. Abraham argues that innocent people should not be punished merely because they live near the wicked.
“Dust and ashes” is a biblical expression of humility and human frailty, not a literal description of Abraham. The same phrase also appears in the Book of Job.

The negotiation ends with the number ten, after Abraham repeatedly asks for mercy for the city. His persistence teaches that a person may raise moral questions and seek justice even before the highest authority.
